items.title: Section: Mindfulness of the Body Through Ultimate Truth — Neither Grasping the Body as Real Nor Denying It Into Nothing

items.zh: 云何菩薩於大乘理趣三十七種菩提分法如實了知？謂諸菩薩，能於其身住循身觀，不於其身分別有性，亦不分別一切種類都無有性。又於其身遠離言說自性、法性如實了知，當知名依勝義理趣，能於其身住循身觀，修習念住。
items.en: How do bodhisattvas correctly and thoroughly know the thirty-seven factors of awakening according to the great vehicle's own approach? Bodhisattvas who, abiding in mindfulness observing the body as such, never conceptually construct the body as possessing a fixed nature, nor conceptually construct it as possessing no nature of any kind whatsoever — and who correctly and thoroughly know the body's own reality-nature, free of any verbally expressed nature — one should understand this to be called cultivating the establishment of mindfulness through the ultimate approach, abiding in mindfulness observing the body as such.

items.title: Section: Mindfulness of the Body Through Conventional Truth, and the Same Double Approach Extended to Every Remaining Factor of Awakening

items.zh: 若諸菩薩隨順無量安立理趣妙智而轉，當知名依世俗理趣，能於其身住循身觀，修習念住。如於其身住循身觀，修習念住，如是所餘一切念住、所餘一切菩提分法，當知亦爾。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who follow the wondrous wisdom of the boundless, name-based conventional approach — one should understand this to be called cultivating the establishment of mindfulness through the conventional approach, abiding in mindfulness observing the body as such. Just as mindfulness observing the body as such is cultivated in this way, one should understand that all the remaining establishments of mindfulness, and all the remaining factors of awakening, are cultivated in exactly the same way.

items.title: Section: The Four Noble Truths Reconceived — Ultimate and Conventional Approaches to Suffering, Its Cause, Its Cessation, and the Path, Closing the Ninth Topic

items.zh: 如是菩薩，於身等法不分別苦、不分別集、不分別此所作斷滅、不分別此得滅因道。又即於此遠離言說自性、法性，若苦法性、若集法性、若滅法性、若道法性，如實了知。當知名依勝義理趣，修菩提分為所依止，緣諦修習。若諸菩薩隨順無量安立理趣妙智而轉，當知名依世俗理趣，緣諦修習。
items.en: In this way, bodhisattvas, regarding the body and the other establishments of mindfulness, do not conceptually construct suffering, do not conceptually construct its cause, do not conceptually construct the cessation brought about through practice, and do not conceptually construct the path that is the cause of attaining that cessation. Furthermore, regarding exactly these truths, freed of conventionally-labelled nature, they correctly and thoroughly know the underlying nature beyond words belonging to suffering, to its cause, to cessation, and to the path. One should understand this to be called taking the ultimate approach as one's basis in cultivating the factors of awakening, practising by way of the truths. Bodhisattvas who follow the wondrous wisdom of the boundless, name-based conventional approach — one should understand this to be called practising by way of the truths through the conventional approach.

items.title: Section: Calming and Insight Defined — Calming as Freedom From All Discrimination, Insight as Both the Wisdom That Directly Realises and the Wisdom That Returns to Explain

items.zh: 此中菩薩即於諸法無所分別，當知名止。若於諸法勝義理趣如實真智，及於無量安立理趣世俗妙智，當知名觀。
items.en: Here, a bodhisattva's mind resting free of all discrimination towards every phenomenon — one should understand this to be called calming. The genuinely realised wisdom directly penetrating the ultimate approach to every phenomenon, together with the wondrous wisdom skilfully engaging the boundless, name-based conventional approach — one should understand this to be called insight.

items.title: Section: Calming's Fourfold Unfolding — From Investigation-Led Approach Through Effortless Freedom From Elaboration to Resting in the Sameness of All Phenomena

items.zh: 此中菩薩略有四行，當知名止。一、勝義世俗智前行；二、勝義世俗智果；三、普於一切戲論想中無功用轉；四、即於如是離言唯事，由無有相無所分別，其心寂靜，趣向一切法平等性、一味實性。由此四行，是諸菩薩止道運轉，漸次乃至能證無上正等菩提智見圓滿。
items.en: Here, bodhisattvas' calming has, in brief, four aspects. First, calming led by wisdom regarding ultimate and conventional truth. Second, calming as the fruit of that wisdom regarding ultimate and conventional truth. Third, calming operating effortlessly, universally, amid every conceptual elaboration. Fourth, calming resting precisely in this freedom from words, in mere dependently arisen fact alone, the mind, through being free of characteristics and free of discrimination, growing still and inclining towards the sameness and single, genuine nature of all phenomena. Through these four aspects, bodhisattvas' calming operates and unfolds, progressing gradually all the way to the complete perfection of supreme, correct awakening's own wisdom and vision.

items.title: Section: Insight's Fourfold Unfolding Closes the Tenth Topic — Freedom From Exaggerating and From Denying, and Skilful Investigation Across Boundless Phenomena

items.zh: 此中菩薩略有四行，當知名觀。謂即四行止道前行，於一切法遠離增益不正執邊，遠離損減不正執邊，及與隨順無量諸法，差別安立理趣妙觀。由此四行，是諸菩薩觀道運轉，漸次乃至能證無上正等菩提智見圓滿。是名略說菩薩止觀。
items.en: Here, bodhisattvas' insight has, in brief, four aspects. First, insight taking those same four aspects of the path of calming as its own necessary basis. Second, insight freeing itself, regarding every phenomenon, from the extreme of incorrectly exaggerating existence. Third, insight freeing itself, regarding every phenomenon, from the extreme of incorrectly denying existence. Fourth, insight skilfully investigating, in accordance with the boundless variety of phenomena, their distinct, name-based approaches. Through these four aspects, bodhisattvas' insight operates and unfolds, progressing gradually all the way to the complete perfection of supreme, correct awakening's own wisdom and vision. This is, in brief, what is called a bodhisattva's calming and insight.

items.title: Section: Skilful Means Opens — Twelve Kinds, Six Turned Inward Towards Realising the Teaching Oneself, Six Turned Outward Towards Maturing Beings

items.zh: 云何菩薩方便善巧？當知略說有十二種。依內修證一切佛法，有其六種；依外成熟一切有情，亦有六種。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's skilful means? One should understand that this is, in brief, of twelve kinds: six belonging to realising the entire teaching by way of inward cultivation, and six belonging to maturing all sentient beings by way of outward activity.

items.title: Section: The Six Inward-Turned Skilful Means — Three Paired Foundations Behind Refusing Nirvāṇa, Staying Unstained in Saṃsāra, and Blazing Diligence

items.zh: 云何依內修證一切佛法六種方便善巧？一者、菩薩於諸有情悲心俱行，顧戀不捨；二者、菩薩於一切行如實遍知；三者、菩薩恒於無上正等菩提所有妙智，深心欣樂；四者、菩薩顧戀有情為依止故，不捨生死；五者、菩薩於一切行如實遍知為依止故，輪轉生死而心不染；六者、菩薩欣樂佛智為依止故，熾然精進。當知是名菩薩依內修證一切佛法六種方便善巧。
items.en: What are the six kinds of skilful means belonging to realising the entire teaching by way of inward cultivation? First, bodhisattvas hold a mind joined with compassion towards sentient beings, cherishing them and unable to abandon them. Second, bodhisattvas correctly and thoroughly know every conditioned activity exactly as it is. Third, bodhisattvas constantly delight deeply in the wondrous wisdom belonging to supreme, correct awakening. Fourth, taking their cherishing of sentient beings as their basis, bodhisattvas do not abandon birth and death. Fifth, taking their thorough knowledge of every conditioned activity as their basis, bodhisattvas wander through birth and death without their mind becoming stained. Sixth, taking their delight in the Buddha's own wisdom as their basis, bodhisattvas sustain blazing diligence. One should understand this to be called the six kinds of skilful means belonging to a bodhisattva's realisation of the entire teaching by way of inward cultivation.

items.title: Section: The Six Outward-Turned Skilful Means Named — From the Smallest Seed of Merit to Beings Who Have Already Fully Ripened

items.zh: 云何依外成熟一切有情六種方便善巧？一者、菩薩方便善巧，能令有情以少善根感無量果；二者、菩薩方便善巧，能令有情少用功力，引攝廣大無量善根；三者、菩薩方便善巧，於佛聖教憎背有情，除其恚惱；四者、菩薩方便善巧，於佛聖教處中有情，令其趣入；五者、菩薩方便善巧，於佛聖教已趣入者，令其成熟；六者、菩薩方便善巧，於佛聖教已成熟者，令得解脫。
items.en: What are the six kinds of skilful means belonging to maturing all sentient beings by way of outward activity? First, a bodhisattva's skilful means enabling beings to reap boundless fruit from only a small wholesome root. Second, a bodhisattva's skilful means enabling beings, expending only minimal effort, to gather in vast, boundless wholesome roots. Third, a bodhisattva's skilful means removing hostility from beings who actively resent the Buddha's noble teaching. Fourth, a bodhisattva's skilful means drawing beings who remain neutral towards the Buddha's noble teaching into genuine entry. Fifth, a bodhisattva's skilful means maturing beings who have already entered the Buddha's noble teaching. Sixth, a bodhisattva's skilful means bringing beings who have already matured within the Buddha's noble teaching to actual liberation.

items.title: Section: The Smallest Gift, Given Even to the Meanest Field, Yields Boundless Fruit — the First Outward Skilful Means

items.zh: 云何菩薩方便善巧，令諸有情以少善根感無量果？謂諸菩薩方便善巧，勸諸有情捨微劣物，乃至最下唯一麨團，施鄙穢田乃至蠢動傍生之類，作是施已，迴求無上正等菩提。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's skilful means enabling beings to reap boundless fruit from only a small wholesome root? Bodhisattvas skilfully persuade beings to give away even a trivial, humble object, down to nothing more than a single small ball of roasted flour, offering it even to a mean, impure field of merit, down to a lowly, mindlessly stirring animal — and, having made this offering, to dedicate it towards supreme, correct awakening.

items.zh: 如是善根，物田雖下，由迴向力，感無量果。

blocks.text: The bodhisattva holds every factor of awakening in two ways at once, ultimately and conventionally. Then calming and insight, and the opening of skilful means.

"They never construct the body as having a fixed nature, nor as having no nature of any kind." Master Cháng Bǎi: in short, neither exaggeration nor denial. The eye, ear, and other faculties established in the body are mere verbal labels without real substance.

Master Cháng Bǎi: Kuiji explains this conventional approach as subsequently attained wisdom. Venerable Miào Jìng: the ultimate approach contemplates emptiness; the conventional approach contemplates provisional names.

"They do not conceive suffering, its cause, the cessation brought about by practice, or the path to it." Master Cháng Bǎi: their verbal nature is unfindable, yet their nature beyond words is not nonexistent.

"Being free of discrimination towards all phenomena is calming; true wisdom of the ultimate approach together with wondrous [subsequent] wisdom is insight." Venerable Miào Jìng: taking the breath as object and resting the mind there without discrimination is calming.

The third: operating effortlessly and universally amid every conceptual elaboration. Venerable Miào Jìng: here wisdom comes first, then calming, though either may precede the other. Master Cháng Bǎi: Mahāyāna calming contains insight; calming is the fruit of wisdom.

To say that dependent things simply do not exist would deny the dependent nature: hence "denial". Venerable Miào Jìng: the boundless causal process of the dependent nature is illusion-like yet vividly present. Master Cháng Bǎi: cling neither to existence nor to emptiness.
"Six for realising the entire dharma inwardly, six for maturing all beings outwardly."

"Taking their cherishing of beings as basis, bodhisattvas do not abandon birth and death." Venerable Miào Jìng: because the bodhisattva sees there is no such thing, they are not stained; the arhat instead observes impermanence, which still treats things as existing. Master Cháng Bǎi: seeing deluded beings kill, steal, and lie and fall into the lower realms, compassion grows.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the "neutral" are beings who neither deeply believe nor disbelieve Buddhism. Venerable Miào Jìng: not hostile to the dharma, but not yet drawn in.

Giving something humble, down to one ball of roasted flour, to a mean field, even an animal, and dedicating it to supreme awakening, bears boundless fruit. Venerable Miào Jìng warned: the dedication is powerful only if the heart is in it; merely reciting the words is not enough.

Today's pattern is the heart of fascicle 45: neither "it is real" nor "it is nothing". The body, the truths, even saṃsāra are held both ways, which is why the bodhisattva can stay in the world without being stained by it.

quiz.q: Contemplating the body by the ultimate approach, which two conceptions does the bodhisattva avoid?
options: conceiving the body as having a nature, or as having no nature at all
quiz.why: "They never construct the body as having a fixed nature, nor as having no nature of any kind." Master Cháng Bǎi: in short, neither grasp at existence nor fall into annihilation and grasping at emptiness.

quiz.q: Practising by way of the truths through the ultimate approach, what does the bodhisattva not conceive regarding the body and so on?
options: suffering, its cause, the cessation, the path to it
quiz.why: "They do not conceive suffering, its cause, the cessation brought about by practice, or the path to it." Master Cháng Bǎi: knowing the verbally established body, feeling, mind, and phenomena are unfindable is "not conceiving suffering." Venerable Miào Jìng: together, body, feeling, mind, and phenomena are the truth of suffering.

quiz.q: How does the treatise define calming and insight?
options: no discrimination towards phenomena is calming; true wisdom of the ultimate plus wondrous conventional wisdom is insight
quiz.why: "Being free of discrimination towards all phenomena is calming; true wisdom of the ultimate approach together with wondrous conventional wisdom is insight." Venerable Miào Jìng: one is the provisional-name (Yogācāra) contemplation, the other the signless contemplation of emptiness.

quiz.q: What is the third of calming's four aspects?
options: operating effortlessly amid all conceptual elaboration
quiz.why: Third: operating effortlessly, universally, amid every conceptual elaboration. Venerable Miào Jìng: "operating effortlessly" means no elaborating thoughts stir — the mind is pure.

quiz.q: How many kinds of skilful means are there, and how are they divided?
options: twelve: six inward for realising the dharma, six outward for maturing beings
quiz.why: "Twelve kinds: six for realising the entire dharma inwardly, six for maturing all beings outwardly." Venerable Miào Jìng: "inward" is the bodhisattva's own calming and insight; "outward" is beings.

quiz.q: Among the inward means, "not abandoning birth and death" is based on what?
quiz.why: "Fourth, taking their cherishing of beings as basis, bodhisattvas do not abandon birth and death." Venerable Miào Jìng: a bodhisattva could practice alone, ignoring beings' suffering — but cannot; they stay in birth and death to accompany beings.

quiz.q: To reap boundless fruit from a small root, what giving does the treatise give as example?
options: giving a humble thing, even one ball of roasted flour, to a mean field, even an animal, then dedicating it to supreme awakening
quiz.why: Giving a humble thing, down to a single ball of roasted flour, to a mean field, even a stirring animal, and dedicating it to supreme awakening. Venerable Miào Jìng: barley meal roasted in a pan, pressed into a ball.
